title: Agent loop manifest
description: Per-repo declaration of everything the stack-agnostic prompt pack needs to know. The prompts, hooks, gates and skills in this template contain NO stack-specific commands; they resolve every command through this file. A subscribing repo ships exactly one of these at its root as agent-loop.manifest.yml.

schema.description: Manifest schema version. Bumped only for breaking shape changes.

pack_version.description: The prompt-pack version this repo is currently synced to. sync/check-pack-version.js compares this against the template's VERSION and opens a re-render PR when the template is ahead — updates are inherited by re-rendering the pack against this manifest, not by hand-adapting a copy. This is the pin that makes propagation pull-based, and the version check-render-equivalence.js renders against.

shared_clone.description: Absolute path to the ONE clone that concurrent sessions share. hooks/block-shared-clone-git.js refuses every mutating git verb aimed here. Mutating a shared clone from a session has corrupted concurrent work in practice (ai-questions, 2026-07-10 and 2026-W29) — this is not a theoretical guard. NOT required at the top level: a freshly spawned repo has no local clone yet, and the path is machine-specific. The shared-clone-guard capability declares it in its own `requires`, so check-capabilities.js enforces it exactly when it matters.

worktrees_rel.description: Session worktree root, relative to shared_clone. Paths under it are SANCTIONED workspaces and are explicitly not treated as the shared clone.

integration.description: The branch loops may merge to autonomously. All PRs target this.

production.description: Never merged to by any loop, under any circumstance.

integration_deploys_to.description: Human-readable name of what an integration merge deploys to, e.g. 'staging'. REQUIRED: prompts quote it unconditionally when telling a reviewer what is already live, so omitting it ships a dangling placeholder. If a merge deploys nothing, say 'nothing' — an explicit 'nothing' is a fact the reviewer can use; a missing key is a hole in the sentence. Leaving it WRONG is how a reviewer ends up reviewing the wrong stream.

commands.description: THE stack-agnostic seam. Every command any prompt, skill, or gate tells an agent to run is declared here and referenced by KEY, never inlined. gates/verify-affordances.js executes each one and fails if it does not run — the deterministic answer to a prompt naming a check that has silently done nothing for weeks. `gate` and `carve_out` are REQUIRED KEYS because prompts across the pack reference them unconditionally; set either to null if the repo genuinely lacks it, but SAY SO. Requiring the key while permitting a null value is deliberate — it makes absence a declaration rather than an omission, which is the difference between a decision and an oversight.

gate.description: The fast, path-aware pre-push gate. The single command an agent runs before claiming a change is verified.

test_real.description: Real-execution tier (not mocks). If a repo has one, prompts MUST distinguish it from test_unit — a green mock suite proves mock-level behavior only.

lint.description: Set to null when the repo has no working linter. Declaring null is REQUIRED and is strictly better than naming a broken one: verify-affordances.js will then stop prompts from citing lint as a completed check.

cantfail.description: Detector for tests that cannot fail (no unconditional assertions).

carve_out.description: Classifies a path as high-risk. Must be RUN, never re-derived from prose — a hand-written carve-out list that drifted narrower than the gate is a recorded cause of unlabeled high-risk merges (ai-questions #779/#780).

agent_run.description: How to invoke the agent harness non-interactively on a prompt file, for measurement rather than for work. Read by evals/run-eval.js, which substitutes {prompt_file}. REQUIRED by the eval-corpus capability: without it, behavioural prompt findings cannot be measured and therefore must not ship. This key was missing here until 2026-W31 while run-eval.js and capabilities.json both already referenced it, which made eval-corpus impossible to enable without failing schema validation — and so made every behavioural finding permanently unshippable in every subscriber.

carve_outs.description: Advisory mirror of the high-risk surface for hooks that warn at edit time. NOT authoritative — commands.carve_out is. Kept only so a warning can fire before a command is available.

governance_files.description: Files the loop must never autonomously author or auto-merge — the rules that bind it. A loop able to rewrite its own constraints has no constraints.

blocked_when_open.description: Issue numbers that, while OPEN, mean a capability is structurally unavailable (e.g. a review-quota outage). Loops read these BEFORE spending a metered resource, rather than inferring the mode from how a result looks.

log_issue.description: The standing issue in THIS repo where the daily review posts each run's summary as a comment and where the Director reads them. OPTIONAL but every prompt that names it will leave an unresolved placeholder until it is declared — which is the intended nudge: the review has no other durable destination, and until 2026-08-15 the pack template hardcoded its own repo's issue number here, so every subscriber that rendered it was told to post to an issue in another repository.

hotline_trigger_id.description: ID of a poke-only scheduler Routine (no cron, no run_once_at — it fires only on demand) that a blocked loop run fires via the scheduler's fire_trigger tool for same-hour triage, instead of waiting for the weekly governance pass. The triage session it spawns holds loop-level authority only. OPTIONAL: when absent, the escalation-hotline prompt section renders away and label-and-wait remains the loop's only escalation path.

human_gate_scope.description: What the human-gate label MEANS here, because two live subscribers disagree and both are right for themselves. `integration`: a PR carrying the label may not merge into branches.integration until a human clears it — a merge past it is a guardrail breach (the pack's original semantics; ai-questions). `production`: the label marks a change that needs a human before it is PROMOTED to branches.production, and does NOT hold an integration merge (lifelift-mobile-backend, whose develop-merges are autonomous by design and whose owner gates only prod). Prompts render the value inline and apply the matching rule. OPTIONAL; when absent, prompts that name it leave an unresolved placeholder rather than guessing — the earlier state, where the pack silently assumed `integration`, was the fatal contradiction the adoption diff found.

escalation.description: Escalation and human-gate labels. Both label keys are REQUIRED because prompts reference them unconditionally; a manifest omitting one ships a prompt with a dangling placeholder.

origin.description: Back-link to the control plane that specified this project, written by bootstrap.js from project.yml. Carries `ideaId`, the control-plane `repo`, and `portfolioIssue`. Kept in the manifest as well as the README because a monthly checkpoint reads the spawned repo alongside its spec to ask whether the built scope is still the specced scope — and a machine-readable link survives a README rewrite that a prose one does not.

capabilities.description: Which pack features this repo installs. Either a list of enabled ids, or an object mapping id -> boolean. Prefer the OBJECT form and record deliberate declines as `false`: an explicit false is a decision, an omission is an oversight, and gates/check-capabilities.js can only tell them apart if you say so. Validated against capabilities.json, which carries each feature's maturity, the condition under which it applies, and when to skip it.

current.description: Model the loop runs on, e.g. 'claude-opus-5'. review/ compares this against the reviewer's validated-against field and marks behavioral rules stale on mismatch instead of silently trusting them.

commit_trailer.description: Trailer appended to every commit the loop authors, e.g. 'Co-Authored-By: ...'. REQUIRED: the loop prompt's hard constraints reference it unconditionally, and attribution that silently stops being applied is the kind of gap nobody notices until an audit.

accepted.description: Other model ids whose attribution is valid here, beyond `current`. OPTIONAL, and it exists because `current` was modelled as a constant and is not one: a session can be moved to a different model server-side, mid-run, with nobody having decided anything. check-model-attribution accepts a trailer naming `current` OR any id listed here; a trailer naming a model in neither still fails, and a missing trailer still fails. Do NOT list models you might someday adopt — list what actually produces work here, because review/ still compares only `current` against validated-against, so every id added here is one whose behavioural claims nothing re-validates.

model.description: Which model the loop runs on, and how its commits are attributed. REQUIRED at the top level: `current` is what review/ compares against the reviewer's validated-against field, and without it a model upgrade silently invalidates every behavioural rule with nothing to detect it.

render_overrides.description: Structured declared overrides applied by renderPrompt AFTER rendering, at any pin, whether the prompt is committed or inherited at run time (issue #113; the unbuilt half of #12). A subscriber's local rule lives HERE as data — which file, which section, what text, on whose authority — never as a hand-edited line in a rendered copy: a byte-exact re-render deleted an owner-enabled review rule that lived that way (#85). An override whose section the template no longer has makes the render THROW; a stale override is drift the render refuses rather than silently drops.

file.description: Template path as the pack names it, e.g. prompts/loop-monitor.md (basename accepted).

section.description: Heading line to act on, matched by prefix against the RENDERED heading text; must match exactly one heading (e.g. "## STAGE 2").

mode.description: replace = the body under the heading (heading kept); append = after the body; prepend = right after the heading; remove = heading and body.

text.description: The local rule, verbatim. Ignored for remove.

why.description: Why this repo differs — the documented unique need or the remediation drift, for the reader and C17.

authority.description: Who decided it and when — an owner quote with date, or the Director verdict that recorded it. Not interpreted; the C6 accounting reads it.

cwd.description: Directory to run in, relative to repo root.

probe.description: A COMPLETE cheap command (not a suffix) that verify-affordances.js runs to prove the tool RESOLVES — e.g. 'npx --no-install eslint --version'. Required whenever 'run' contains a {file} placeholder. Distinguishes 'the check ran and found problems' from 'the check could not run at all' — the distinction whose absence let a dead linter pass as a passing gate for ~25 days.

oneOf.description: Explicitly absent. Required rather than omitted, so absence is a declaration instead of an oversight.
